description:
Capture an app's UI as a numbered list of elements (refs e1, e2…) that other tools act on.
Use it before acting and whenever the UI may have changed. Refs stay valid across snapshots while
their element exists (unchanged elements keep their ref; numbers are never reused).
Params: app / window_id (default: the frontmost app's focused window); mode: auto (default: the
accessibility tree, plus OCR text elements o1… when the tree is poor), interactive (actionable
elements only), full (every element), text (reading view), vision (always add OCR elements);
max_elements / offset to page (or snapshot_id + offset to page an existing snapshot without
re-capturing); include_screenshot / annotate (image with refs drawn on it).
Returns one line per element (ref, role, name, value, states, center point), the focused element,
the menu bar, app kind and AX quality, and paging info; structuredContent has every field.
Errors: APP_NOT_FOUND, WINDOW_NOT_FOUND, SNAPSHOT_NOT_FOUND, PERMISSION_ACCESSIBILITY,
BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, TIMEOUT.

annotate.description: Return a screenshot with element refs drawn on it (implies include_screenshot).

app.description: Target app: name ('Notes'), bundle id ('com.apple.Notes') or pid. Default: the frontmost app.

include_screenshot.description: Also return a screenshot of the window.

mode.description: auto | interactive | full | text | vision (see the tool description).

offset.description: Index of the first element to return (paging).

snapshot_id.description: Page through this existing snapshot instead of capturing again.

window_id.description: Window id from list_windows; scopes the call to that window.

name: snapshot
title: Snapshot an app's UI

description:
Take a screenshot of a display, a window, an app's front window or a screen region.
Use it to see what the accessibility tree cannot show (images, canvases, layout); prefer snapshot
for acting. Params: display_id | window_id | app | rect [x, y, width, height] in points (at most
one; default: the main display), max_edge (longest edge in pixels, default 1280), format.
Returns the image plus a screenshot_id and its scale: to click something you see in it, pass its
pixel x/y with coordinate_space="screenshot" and that screenshot_id. Apps on the deny list are
left out of the image. Errors: PERMISSION_SCREEN_RECORDING, DISPLAY_NOT_FOUND, WINDOW_NOT_FOUND,
APP_NOT_FOUND, BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, TIMEOUT.

app.description: Capture the front window of this app (name, bundle id or pid).

display_id.description: Display id from list_displays. Default: the main display.

max_edge.description: Longest image edge in pixels (default from config, 1280).

rect.description: Region [x, y, width, height] in screen points (e.g. a frame from a snapshot).

window_id.description: Window id from list_windows; scopes the call to that window.

name: screenshot
title: Take a screenshot

description:
Map an app in one call: its windows, menu bar (top-level menus with item counts), toolbar buttons,
tabs, sidebar sections, scroll areas, open dialogs and the focused element, plus how well AXPilot can
drive it (app kind, accessibility quality, strategies, tips).
Call it first for an unfamiliar app, then snapshot for the full element list. Params: app / window_id.
Returns a compact overview with refs (usable with click, read, scroll…) and the snapshot_id they belong
to. Errors: APP_NOT_FOUND, WINDOW_NOT_FOUND, PERMISSION_ACCESSIBILITY, BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, TIMEOUT.

app.description: Target app: name ('Notes'), bundle id ('com.apple.Notes') or pid. Default: the frontmost app.

window_id.description: Window id from list_windows; scopes the call to that window.

name: explore
title: Explore an app

description:
Wait until something happens on screen (polling, at most 60 s), instead of sleeping and guessing.
Conditions: element (an element matching query/role appears; returns its ref), element_gone,
window (a window whose title contains query, or any window of app, opens), app_running (query =
app name or bundle id), text_visible (query appears as text; ocr=true also checks pixels), idle
(the app's UI stops changing for 0.5 s), duration (just wait timeout_ms).
Params: condition, query, role, app (default: frontmost app), timeout_ms (default 10000).
Returns what matched and how long it took. Errors: TIMEOUT (the condition never became true:
take a snapshot to see why), INVALID_ARGUMENT, BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, PERMISSION_ACCESSIBILITY.

app.description: Target app: name ('Notes'), bundle id ('com.apple.Notes') or pid. Default: the frontmost app.

condition.description: What to wait for (see the tool description).

ocr.description: text_visible only: also look for the text with OCR (slower).

query.description: Element text, window title, app name/bundle id or text (depends on condition).

role.description: Element role filter (button, field, row…) for element conditions.

timeout_ms.description: Give up after this many ms (max 60000); for duration, how long to wait.

name: wait_for
title: Wait for a condition

description:
Report AXPilot's state: version, engine, macOS version, permissions (Accessibility, Screen
Recording), whether the user paused it (kill switch), the input lock, the active profile and
enabled tools, rate limit and confirmation mode.
Use it first when tools fail with permission errors, or to check what this server can do.
name: status
title: AXPilot status

description:
Click an element (by ref) or a point.
Prefer ref from the latest snapshot: AXPilot presses it through accessibility (works even when the
window is in the background, without moving the pointer) and falls back to a real mouse click.
Params: ref | x+y (coordinate_space "points" or "screenshot" + screenshot_id), button
(left|right|middle), count (2 = double-click), modifiers (e.g. ["cmd"] to add to a selection),
strategy (auto|ax|mouse), report (diff|snapshot|none).
Returns how it clicked and what changed (new/removed elements, focus and value changes) with the
new snapshot_id. Errors: STALE_REF (take a new snapshot), ELEMENT_NOT_ACTIONABLE (disabled or
covered), BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, USER_ACTIVE, PAUSED_BY_USER, INVALID_ARGUMENT.

coordinate_space.description: "points" (screen points) or "screenshot" (pixels of the screenshot given by screenshot_id, or the latest one).

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the action, e.g. ["cmd"] to add to a selection.

ref.description: Element ref from the latest snapshot, e.g. "e12" (or an OCR ref "o3"). Give either ref or x/y.

report.description: What to return after acting: "diff" (what changed, default), "snapshot" (the whole new snapshot) or "none" (fastest).

screenshot_id.description: Screenshot the pixel coordinates refer to ("c_ab12"). Default: the latest.

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the ref belongs to. Default: the latest snapshot.

x.description: X coordinate (with y). Screen points by default.

y.description: Y coordinate (with x). Screen points by default.

name: click
title: Click

description:
Type text into a field (by ref) or into whatever has keyboard focus.
With ref, AXPilot focuses the field first. It sets the text through accessibility in native apps,
types real keystrokes in web views, Electron, Java and Qt apps (they ignore accessibility edits),
and pastes long text (restoring your clipboard afterwards).
Params: text, ref (optional), clear (replace the field's content), submit (press Return after),
strategy (auto|ax_value|keystrokes|paste), report.
Errors: SECURE_INPUT_ACTIVE (a password prompt or secure terminal blocks typing),
BLOCKED_BY_POLICY (password fields, Terminal unless the shell tool is enabled), STALE_REF,
ELEMENT_NOT_ACTIONABLE, USER_ACTIVE, PAUSED_BY_USER.

ref.description: Element ref from the latest snapshot, e.g. "e12" (or an OCR ref "o3"). Give either ref or x/y.

report.description: What to return after acting: "diff" (what changed, default), "snapshot" (the whole new snapshot) or "none" (fastest).

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the ref belongs to. Default: the latest snapshot.

strategy.description: How to enter the text (default auto).

name: type_text
title: Type text

description:
Press keyboard shortcuts or keys, e.g. "cmd+s", "cmd+shift+t", "escape", "tab", or a sequence
"cmd+a delete". Keys go to the frontmost app (pass app to bring one forward first).
Names: cmd, option, ctrl, shift, fn; return, escape, tab, space, delete, forward_delete, up, down,
left, right, home, end, page_up, page_down, f1-f20, plus, minus, any character.
Params: keys, repeat (1-50), app, report. Prefer select_menu for menu commands (it works without
knowing the shortcut). Errors: SECURE_INPUT_ACTIVE, INVALID_ARGUMENT (unknown key),
BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, USER_ACTIVE, PAUSED_BY_USER.

app.description: Target app: name ('Notes'), bundle id ('com.apple.Notes') or pid. Default: the frontmost app.

keys.description: A combo or a space-separated sequence, e.g. "cmd+shift+t" or "cmd+a delete".

repeat.description: Press the whole sequence this many times.

report.description: What to return after acting: "diff" (what changed, default), "snapshot" (the whole new snapshot) or "none" (fastest).

name: press_keys
title: Press keys

description:
Scroll a list, table, web page or text area: by lines or pages, to the top or bottom, or until an
element is visible.
Target: ref (a scroll area, or any element inside one), x/y (a point; coordinate_space / screenshot_id
as for click), or neither (the largest scroll area of app's window). direction (up|down|left|right),
amount + unit (lines|pages; a page is ~80% of the visible area), to (top|bottom), scroll_into_view
(ref of an element to bring into view).
Returns moved, at_end (cannot scroll further that way), scrolls, and what changed (report:
diff|snapshot|none) with the new snapshot_id. For long content prefer read (collects everything)
or find(scroll=true). Errors: STALE_REF, ELEMENT_NOT_ACTIONABLE (nothing scrollable),
BLOCKED_BY_POLICY, USER_ACTIVE, PAUSED_BY_USER, INVALID_ARGUMENT.

app.description: Target app: name ('Notes'), bundle id ('com.apple.Notes') or pid. Default: the frontmost app.

coordinate_space.description: "points" (screen points) or "screenshot" (pixels of the screenshot given by screenshot_id, or the latest one).

ref.description: Ref of a scroll area, list, table, web area or text area (or of an element inside one), e.g. "e13".

report.description: What to return after acting: "diff" (what changed, default), "snapshot" (the whole new snapshot) or "none" (fastest).

screenshot_id.description: Screenshot the pixel coordinates refer to ("c_ab12"). Default: the latest.

scroll_into_view.description: Ref of an element to scroll into view (no other target needed).

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot the ref belongs to. Default: the latest snapshot.

to.description: "top" or "bottom": scroll all the way (ignores direction/amount).

x.description: X coordinate (with y). Screen points by default.

y.description: Y coordinate (with x). Screen points by default.

name: scroll
title: Scroll

description:
Launch, activate (bring to the front), hide, unhide, quit or force-quit an app.
Use it to switch apps instead of clicking the Dock. Params: action; name (app name such as "Notes",
bundle id such as "com.apple.Notes", or for launch an .app path).
Returns the app afterwards (pid, frontmost, hidden). quit asks the app to quit (it may ask to save
first); force_quit kills it without saving and asks the user to confirm.
Errors: APP_NOT_FOUND, BLOCKED_BY_POLICY (protected apps), USER_DENIED, INVALID_ARGUMENT.

action.description: launch | activate | hide | unhide | quit | force_quit.

name.description: App name ("Notes"), bundle id ("com.apple.Notes") or, for launch, an .app path.

name: app
title: Manage an app
